# Data and teaching purpose

Import **STeLLA_merged_binary_SES.xlsx**, first worksheet, through RStudio's
**Import Dataset > From Excel** menu. Set the imported object's name to
**STeLLA_merged_binary_SES**. The new `SES_high` column is numeric: **0 = Low SES,
1 = High SES**.

In this short lab, test whether the within-school High-versus-Low SES difference
in POST varies by treatment condition. Use the 2,823 complete students in
77 schools. Work through the code and answer the questions at the end.

# Setup and analytic sample

If needed, install `dplyr`, `lmerTest`, and `rmarkdown` once in the Console before
running this document. There are no installation commands in the analytic chunks.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
#Chunk 1

library(dplyr)
library(lmerTest)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)

student_data <- STeLLA_merged_binary_SES |>
  transmute(
    SchoolID = factor(SchoolID), StudentID, PRE, POST,
    TREAT = School_TREAT, MEANPRE = School_MEANPRE,
    SES_high
  ) |>
  filter(complete.cases(SchoolID, StudentID, PRE, POST, TREAT,
                        MEANPRE, SES_high))

stopifnot(
  nrow(student_data) == 2823,
  n_distinct(student_data$StudentID) == 2823,
  n_distinct(student_data$SchoolID) == 77,
  all(student_data$TREAT %in% 0:1),
  all(student_data$SES_high %in% 0:1)
)
print(c(Students = nrow(student_data),
        Schools = n_distinct(student_data$SchoolID)))
with(student_data, table(TREAT, SES_high))
```

# Center the student predictors

PRE and SES are centered within school. TREAT stays uncentered (0/1) so that
the SES coefficient directly gives the high-low difference in comparison schools.
The mean of a binary indicator is a proportion.

```{r centering}
#Chunk 2

student_data <- student_data |>
  group_by(SchoolID) |>
  mutate(
    PRE_w = PRE - mean(PRE),
    SES_school = mean(SES_high),
    SES_w = SES_high - SES_school
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Confirm that centered predictors average to zero within schools.
student_data |>
  group_by(SchoolID) |>
  summarise(Mean_PRE_w = mean(PRE_w), Mean_SES_w = mean(SES_w)) |>
  summarise(Max_abs_PRE = max(abs(Mean_PRE_w)),
            Max_abs_SES = max(abs(Mean_SES_w)))
```

Within one school, moving from Low to High SES always increases `SES_w` by one.


# Fit the models

## Additive model

```{r additive-model}

#Chunk 3 - Main effects
ses_main_effects <- lmer(
  POST ~ PRE_w + TREAT + SES_w + (1 | SchoolID),
  data = student_data
)
summary(ses_main_effects)
```

## Cross-level interaction model

Treatment is a school-level predictor and SES is a student-level predictor.
The product tests whether treatment condition changes the within-school SES gap.

```{r interaction-model}

#Chunk 4 - interaction model
ses_interaction <- lmer(
  POST ~ PRE_w + TREAT * SES_w + (1 | SchoolID),
  data = student_data
)
summary(ses_interaction)
confint(ses_interaction, parm = "TREAT:SES_w", method = "Wald")
```

The fixed interaction allows different SES gaps by treatment condition.
This primary model has random school intercepts, not random SES slopes.

# Simple effects and interpretation

```{r simple-effects}

#Chunk 5

b <- fixef(ses_interaction)

c(
  Comparison_high_minus_low = unname(b["SES_w"]),
  STeLLA_high_minus_low = unname(b["SES_w"] + b["TREAT:SES_w"]),
  Difference_in_SES_gaps = unname(b["TREAT:SES_w"])
)

# Satterthwaite tests and confidence intervals for each high-low contrast.
comparison_contrast <- setNames(rep(0, length(b)), names(b))
comparison_contrast["SES_w"] <- 1
stella_contrast <- comparison_contrast
stella_contrast["TREAT:SES_w"] <- 1

lmerTest::contest1D(ses_interaction, comparison_contrast, confint = TRUE)
lmerTest::contest1D(ses_interaction, stella_contrast, confint = TRUE)
```

# Plot adjusted cell means

This plot holds PRE at the school mean (`PRE_w = 0`) and the school's High SES
proportion at .50. Predictions exclude school-specific random intercepts.


```{r adjusted-cell-means}

#Chunk 6

plot_data <- expand.grid(SES_high = c(0, 1), TREAT = c(0, 1))
plot_data$PRE_w <- 0
plot_data$SES_w <- plot_data$SES_high - 0.5
plot_data$Predicted_POST <- predict(
  ses_interaction, newdata = plot_data, re.form = NA
)
print(plot_data)

plot(
  c(0, 1), plot_data$Predicted_POST[plot_data$TREAT == 0],
  type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = 2, col = "#266785",
  xlim = c(-0.12, 1.12),
  ylim = range(plot_data$Predicted_POST) + c(-2, 2), xaxt = "n",
  xlab = "Simulated SES group", ylab = "Adjusted predicted POST",
  main = "Economic Advantage across Treatment Conditions"
)
lines(
  c(0, 1), plot_data$Predicted_POST[plot_data$TREAT == 1],
  type = "b", pch = 17, lwd = 2, col = "#B04828"
)
axis(1, at = c(0, 1), labels = c("Low SES (0)", "High SES (1)"))
text(
  plot_data$SES_high, plot_data$Predicted_POST,
  labels = sprintf("%.2f", plot_data$Predicted_POST),
  pos = c(1, 1, 3, 3), cex = 0.85
)
legend(
  "topleft", c("Comparison", "STeLLA"),
  col = c("#266785", "#B04828"), pch = c(16, 17), lty = 1, bty = "n"
)
```

# Lab questions

1. Report the `TREAT:SES_w` estimate, standard error, p-value, and confidence interval.
   Does the SES difference vary by treatment condition?
2. Report the estimated High-minus-Low SES difference in each condition.
   Explain the interaction in POST points.
4. Use the labeled plot to explain how both SES differences can be positive
   while the interaction is negative.
